items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1961-01-29
items.q: the leader was named George Morris, a trombone player... We all had, we were taking lessons from this, Sam, for the Perkins.

ctx.x: Where did you go to after Dave Perkins? Did you go to any other teachers?

Well, no. Like I said, this little, this band, they were all fellows older than me because I was just about 18, if I remember well. And they were all the trombone players named George Morris and the trombone players named Thomas Mack. And the clarinet player was named Edmund Washington.

items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1979-12-05
items.q: The Trammer played George Morris... And so we got this job... they used to hire me... So we told him that when we were going, we couldn't take him... we were having trouble with this guy

ctx.x: When did you start playing music professionally for, you know, your first few jobs?

Well I wasn't calling myself a professional before, before 24. I was in ninth grade, 35, right there, F1-0. And these two guys was taking lessons. This man and these guys were married men and everything. They left in the days first. The Trammer played George Morris, and Trump was played Thomas Mack. And the saxophone player, Edmund Washington. I just buried them this year, first part of this year. And they used to get a little job, they used to hire me. They had family and everything. I mean, they were work guys,…
Yeah. So you decided pretty much in Pensacola that, or?

items.title: Emmanuel Sayles Interview, 1959-01-17
items.q: we all left New Orleans together that's what it was yeah on the train... George Morris at that time was the manager of the band... myself on banjo

ctx.x: About how old were you? Can we get that?

Well, it's kind of hard. I should have figured it out, but I was in about fourth or fifth grade. Well, you're quite young. At that time, kids were pretty old. I mean, not like now, you know, so I must have been around about 10 or 11 years old, maybe older than that. Because I can wait and bring in this park. I can remember in 1924, I was just about ready to make it. I hadn't quite, I hadn't even made 18 or close to it. And that was April, like I'm born in January. And that was when, of course, I'm going to get to…

Albert Nicholas was the one that I remember my dad is he played with him with the Silver Leaf Band and they use a violin because my dad at one time had a bass violin I don't know whether it was either with long term but sometime maybe on going to those jobs there was three of them mostly like a bass violin a guitar and sometimes they'd use a mandolin what did Albert Nicholas play I believe no I'm not thinking of Albert Nicholas the one that we know now is the clan that played but this guy I believe played was the…
